subject: Design and Technologies
title: Y7-8 Design and Technologies — Design Cycle
progression_endpoint: Students analyse a need or opportunity, develop and evaluate design criteria collaboratively, generate and test design ideas, select and justify materials and processes, safely produce a designed solution, and evaluate the solution against criteria including sustainability and ethical considerations.

phases.label: Define
phases.checkpoint: Students can analyse a need or opportunity, investigate and select resources with justification, and establish collaboratively developed design criteria including sustainability.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Identify the need, constraints and intended users from a brief; test two materials; select and justify resources with one reason each; develop three design criteria collaboratively including one sustainability criterion.
width_tiers.typical_width: Analyse a need across community contexts; test and compare a range of materials and processes; select resources weighing properties, sustainability and life cycle; develop specific multi-dimensional criteria through consultation; trace the path from analysed need to design direction.
wider: Analyse design opportunities for First Nations Australian communities where place and culture shape the design need
Use survey or consultation to determine user needs and drive resource selection; compare two design directions for the same need
Apply life cycle assessment as a criteria framework; investigate emerging technologies to expand available design options

phases.label: Plan
phases.checkpoint: Students can plan production steps, manage time and cost, and identify risks before production begins.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Identify materials, tools and steps from a drawing; create a plan with three steps, time estimates and responsibilities; identify two project-level risks with contingency strategies.
width_tiers.typical_width: Interpret drawings to develop detailed production procedures; use a digital tool to track tasks, costs and critical dates; identify and plan contingencies for risks across time, resources and scope.
wider: Compare time estimates against actuals to improve future planning
Use digital project management tools to track complex projects; develop contingency plans that adjust scope without compromising design quality

phases.label: Evaluate — existing products
phases.checkpoint: Students can evaluate existing designed solutions against criteria and analyse ethical, sustainability and innovation factors to inform their own design decisions.

waypoints.note: Apply collaboratively developed criteria to analyse existing products — insights inform the design brief.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one existing product against two collaboratively developed criteria; identify one design insight to inform own solution.
width_tiers.typical_width: Evaluate multiple existing products across all criteria; compare what works across cultural and geographic contexts; document insights as design constraints or opportunities.
wider: Compare existing products from different cultural or geographic contexts against the same criteria
Evaluate products at different price or quality tiers and explain how criteria satisfaction varies

phases.label: Design
phases.checkpoint: Students can generate multiple design ideas using varied strategies, test ideas through prototypes, communicate designs using technical drawings, and manage time and cost planning.

waypoints.note: Identify production hazards specific to selected materials and equipment before making begins.
Evaluate and iterate design ideas against criteria during the design process.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Generate two alternative designs using at least one strategy; build and test a prototype for one functional requirement; select materials and processes with justification; identify production hazards; produce an annotated sketch with two technical conventions; evaluate and modify the design against two criteria.
width_tiers.typical_width: Generate alternatives using multiple strategies; develop and test prototypes at different fidelity levels; select and justify resources across materials, tools and processes with sustainability trade-offs; plan for all production hazards; produce technical drawings with scale and symbols; evaluate and iterate against all criteria throughout the design phase.
wider: Consult users or community members and use findings to drive design decisions
Investigate emerging technologies or unfamiliar techniques and justify why they are more appropriate than familiar alternatives
Use peer or user testing to iterate the design; evaluate against accessibility criteria not in the original brief

phases.label: Develop
phases.checkpoint: Students can safely produce a designed solution using justified material and process selections, applying safe and inclusive working practices and managing risks throughout production.

waypoints.note: Managing risks during production — applying planned strategies and responding to unexpected hazards.
Evaluate production decisions during making — adjust plan when circumstances change.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Apply planned risk mitigation during production; respond to one unexpected hazard; apply safe working practices consistently; evaluate one production decision and explain what changed.
width_tiers.typical_width: Apply risk mitigation strategies consistently and document unexpected risks; apply safe, inclusive working practices throughout; evaluate decisions at key points and adjust the plan when circumstances change.
wider: Compare planned vs actual risks to identify unanticipated hazards
Evaluate whether planned mitigation strategies were effective or needed adjustment; reflect on how safety decisions affected production efficiency

phases.label: Evaluate — your solution
phases.checkpoint: Students can evaluate their own designed solution against collaboratively developed criteria, identify improvements, and reflect on how ethical and sustainability factors shaped their design decisions.

waypoints.note: Revisited here — evaluate the finished solution against the criteria developed at Define, informed by earlier analysis of existing products.
Reflect on how safe practice decisions held up during production.
Reflect on how production planning decisions held up — what would change in a future project.

width_tiers.minimum_width: Evaluate the completed solution against two criteria; reflect on one safe practice decision and one production decision; identify one improvement for each.
width_tiers.typical_width: Evaluate across all criteria distinguishing met/partially met/unmet; reflect on how risk identification and planning affected the production experience; identify specific improvements and explain why.
wider: Evaluate how iterative modification throughout improved the final outcome
Compare time and cost estimates against actuals; evaluate whether contingency decisions were worth the trade-offs made
